newsitem.title: UK: RJB down, PowerGen reports weigh.
newsitem.headline: RJB down, PowerGen reports weigh.

text.p: Shares in RJB Mining Plc, trading ex a 12 pence dividend, fell 22-1/2 pence to 410 following press reports which said the company had so far failed to secure new coal supply contracts with electricity generator PowerGen Plc, dealers said.
PowerGen has already signed contracts with other mining companies to cover between a third and a half of its 1998 needs, the Sunday Telegraph and Financial Times said.
No-one at RJB or PowerGen was immediately available to comment.

RJB currently supplies PowerGen and Britain's other main generator, National Power Plc, under long-term contracts at guaranteed prices above world market levels. But these vital deals expire in March 1998.

RJB said earlier it was confident it could win new contracts with its two main clients as it expected the so-called "dash-for gas" to falter with power generators seen keen not to become overdependent on gas.
But PowerGen was now reported to have concluded new coal supply deals with RJB's rivals Midlands Mining and Mining Scotland. The generator is also said to be looking for a major import deal.

The press reports hurt sentiment, but dealers said there was no big selling pressure as RJB, which acquired most of the British Coal collieries in 1994, was widely expecetd to face tough competition from other mining companies.
